title: Synthetic prompt-driven change-detection pipeline with client-side privacy mode
creator: Aisha Njoroge
description:
Goal: Build a production pipeline that runs regression-quality checks per-customer whenever a model or serving configuration changes, while preserving tenant data isolation via a client-side privacy mode. This ticket covers the orchestration, synthetic prompt generation, score aggregation, and gating policies for Dedicated and Private customers.

Problem statement:
- Model/config rollouts occasionally introduce regressions that only manifest on customer-specific patterns. Centralized golden corpora can leak tenant-sensitive signals and are unacceptable for private/Dedicated customers.
- Current evals are global and run infrequently; we need near-real-time detection tied to deployment events.

Proposed solution overview:
1) Synthetic prompt generator (client-assisted) — a lightweight JS/Python library run by the customer (or within VPC) that samples anonymized prompt skeletons from a local reference corpus and expands them into synthetic test prompts using a seeded generator. The generator returns only prompt-level hashes and synthetic prompts (no raw customer PII leaves the tenant).
2) Change-triggering — on any model/config change (model version, quantization profile, batch policy), the control plane triggers per-tenant evaluation jobs that either run in-hosted sandbox (for hosted customers) or inside the customer VPC/on-prem operator (for Private/Dedicated).
3) Scoring and aggregation — lightweight metrics (accuracy proxies, coverage, hallucination signals, token-efficiency) computed locally; only aggregated metrics and differentially-private deltas are reported to Redwood.
4) Gating and automation — policies (fail-open, fail-close, canary, hold rollout) per-customer that can block/roll back deployments automatically when degradation exceeds thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer library prototypes (JS + Python) with API to produce N synthetic prompts from a local seed; includes PII-scrubbing checklist.
- Trigger plumbing implemented: model/config change event -> per-tenant eval job scheduled.
- Local scoring runs produce metrics and a signed summary bundle that can be uploaded; Redwood console can visualize per-tenant summaries within access controls.
- Gating rules configured per-customer; a blocked rollout must be revertable via control-plane action.
- Security review completed and KMS/HSM patterns documented for signing bundles.

Non-goals:
- Building full-fledged customer prompt collectors or shipping customer raw data to Redwood.
- Replacing existing global eval suites — those run in parallel for central benchmarks.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Local vs hosted execution: Local preserves privacy but increases operational surface and support burden for Private customers.
- Synthetic fidelity vs leakage risk: Higher-fidelity synthetic prompts detect subtler regressions but increase chances of accidental privacy exposure. We will favor conservative scrubbing + DP aggregation for reported metrics.

Operational cost estimate:
- Hosted eval runner: ~0.5–1% additional runtime capacity during rollouts; likely batched across tenants.
- Private/Dedicated: customers can opt-in to run inside their capacity; Redwood will provide a lightweight operator and telemetry collector.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/Synthetic+Client-Side+Evals (draft)
- Prototype library repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-synth-client (PR #72)
